name: Central Square Foundation (Founders Pledge)
beneficiaries_note: The countries the notes on the rows its bottom line reads name more than once: India.
summary: Helps Indian state governments run structured teaching of foundational literacy and numeracy. Founders Pledge's page gives under £2.50 per student and gains of 0.29 (numeracy) and 0.43 (literacy) standard deviations; we turn them into income with Founders Pledge's own 2023 education method.

sections.title: Founders Pledge's figures
sections.explainer: Founders Pledge's own figures, as its recommendation page states them. It publishes no spreadsheet for this recommendation, so these are the model's only evaluator rows.

sections.title: Pounds to dollars
sections.explainer: charityevals' step: the page states costs in pounds; we convert at the 2024 average rate.

sections.title: From test scores to units of value
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, using Founders Pledge's own method: its 2023 education report turns a rise in test scores into higher lifetime earnings (19.1% more a year per standard deviation, 17.5% of it kept, from 8 years on for 40 years, shared with the household). The page's figure stops at test scores; we apply the method as its Imagine Worldwide model does.

sections.title: Staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not Founders Pledge's: with credit by share of resources on, staff's pay below what they could earn elsewhere counts as an in-kind contribution and gets its share of the outcome. Off by default.

rows.label: Gain in numeracy (standard deviations)

source.title: Founders Pledge, Central Square Foundation (recommendation page)
source.quote: an average improvement of 0.29 standard deviations in numeracy and 0.43 standard deviations in literacy

rows.explainer: From evaluations by Education Initiatives of over 15,000 students in 10 districts of Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, as the page reports them.

rows.label: Gain in literacy (standard deviations)

source.title: Founders Pledge, Central Square Foundation (recommendation page)
source.quote: an average improvement of 0.29 standard deviations in numeracy and 0.43 standard deviations in literacy

rows.label: Average learning gain (standard deviations)
rows.explainer: Our calculation from the page's two figures: the mean of the two subjects, as education analyses usually summarise a gain in both. Founders Pledge's page doesn't combine them.

rows.label: Cost per student (£, upper bound)

source.title: Founders Pledge, Central Square Foundation (recommendation page)
source.quote: Expanding their district level programs is extremely low cost for a structured pedagogy intervention of this quality—less than £2.50 per student.

rows.explainer: From the page: expanding district programs costs "less than £2.50 per student". We take £2.50, the upper bound, so the result is if anything low.

rows.label: Rise in test scores per pound (standard deviations)
rows.explainer: Our calculation from the page's figures (mean gain over the upper-bound cost); Founders Pledge publishes no per-pound figure.

rows.label: US dollars per pound (2024 average)
Rise in test scores per dollar (standard deviations)
Discount for a non-randomised evaluation
rows.explainer: Our judgment. The gains come from Education Initiatives' comparison of districts, not a randomised trial; the page gives no comparison group or design. Quasi-experimental education evaluations tend to find larger effects than randomised ones, and randomised trials of structured pedagogy mostly find 0.1 to 0.3 standard deviations, against 0.36 here.

rows.label: Share of the gain due to Central Square Foundation's spending
rows.explainer: Our judgment. The £2.50 is what Central Square Foundation spends to expand a district program, but the gain comes from the whole government-run program, and India's national literacy and numeracy mission runs in comparison districts too. If the government spends about as much again (Founders Pledge's Imagine Worldwide model: 1.03 per philanthropic dollar), Central Square Foundation's money is about half the cost, so we credit it with half of the gain, from a quarter to all. With credit by share of resources on, this drops and the government's spending counts as cost instead.

rows.label: Rise in test scores per dollar, credited to Central Square Foundation
Founders Pledge's prior for an education program's effect (standard deviations)
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's 2023 education method doesn't take a measured effect at face value: it averages it with a prior of 0.1 standard deviations (the shared Founders Pledge fact).

rows.label: Weight on the prior
rows.explainer: Our judgment, one value for every Founders Pledge education model whose page doesn't state its shrinking (facts: founders_pledge_2023.prior_weight): 50% on Founders Pledge's prior of 0.1 standard deviations, what Founders Pledge applied to Imagine Worldwide's national scale-up, with 25% (its rule for samples above 2,000) to 75% as the range.

rows.label: Effect after shrinking towards the prior, as a share of the measured effect
rows.explainer: The measured gain, discounted for the evaluation's design, averaged with Founders Pledge's prior, as a share of the measured gain.

rows.label: Rise in test scores per dollar, after shrinking (standard deviations)
Annual salary increase per standard deviation of learning
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's own figure from its 2023 education report (19.1%), shared with its Imagine Worldwide model. The page's figure stops at test scores; this and the rows below are Founders Pledge's own method for turning test scores into income, applied by us.

rows.label: Replicability adjustment
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's 17.5%: how much of that earnings evidence it expects to hold up, from comparing it with the evidence for deworming.

rows.label: Yearly gain in ln(income) per standard deviation
Years until the income gain starts
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's 8 years from primary school to work.

rows.label: Years the income gain lasts
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's 40 working years.

rows.label: Household multiplier
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge counts the gain twice because it is shared with the household.

rows.label: Present value of ln(income) gains per standard deviation, per student
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's formula from its Imagine Worldwide model: the yearly gain paid at the start of each of 40 years, discounted, then discounted again for the 8-year wait. Here at the shared discount rate (Your values); Founders Pledge used 4%, the site's default.

rows.label: Increase in ln(income) per dollar
Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: The income gain valued like every income gain on the site: GiveWell's units of value per unit of ln(consumption) (one unit = doubling one person's income for a year).

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Technical assistance to governments: mostly people. Our judgment; we haven't seen Central Square Foundation's cost breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Researchers, advisers and advocates could typically earn considerably more in consulting or industry. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Government spending on the program per dollar of Central Square Foundation's
rows.explainer: Our judgment: governments pay the teachers, materials and monitoring of the program Central Square Foundation designs and supports. Reference: Founders Pledge's Imagine Worldwide model puts government spending at about 1.03 per philanthropic dollar. Counts only with credit by share of resources on, when every contributor's spending shares the gain.

rows.label: Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per donor dollar
rows.explainer: Units of value per dollar, in GiveWell's units (one unit = a year of doubled income for one person). With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).

native.unit: standard deviations of test scores per £
